eobiont: A hypothetical primordial life-form or chemical precursor to a living organism.
eohippus: An extinct early Eocene mammal (Hyracotherium leporinum), ancestral to the modern horse.
eolith: Crudely chopped flints, believed to be naturally produced by geological processes such as glaciation.
eolithic: of or relating to the early period of the Stone Age marked by the use of eoliths.
eolopile: A metal sphere, containing water, and having two opposing jets, that rotates when the water is boiled
eon: Eternity, the duration of the universe.
eonian: Of or pertaining to an eon
eonism: The pretence of being the opposite sex, especially that by a man of being a woman; transvestism.
eosin: A red, acidic dye commonly used in histological stains.
eosinophil: A white blood cell responsible for combating parasitic infections in the body.
eosinophilia: The condition of having a high concentration of eosinophils (eosinophil granulocytes) in the blood.
eosinophilic: That is readily stained with eosin.
